summary: Prompt human review is supported, alongside and not instead of urgent treatment of the acute illness. At the cutoff, this 94-year-old had arrived at an acute medical unit with fever, productive cough, increased work of breathing, oxygen saturation 88% on air, and right lower-zone air-space change after several months of respiratory symptoms and a marked decline in white cells and neutrophils. The acute infection is a potentially treatable explanation and the record does not establish an irreversible trajectory, but the combination of acute physiological compromise, profound neutropenia, advanced age, and undocumented wishes or escalation planning makes a proportionate priorities-and-contingency conversation appropriate once immediate needs and capacity are assessed.

dataQuality.coverageSummary: The manifest reports successful collection of the single 15-day eligible snapshot, with 38 unique resources, no duplicate visibility, no failed source, and no forced insufficient-evidence safety gate. Clinical coverage is nevertheless narrow: it is not a separately collected full multi-source record, and the snapshot omits important baseline, medication, diagnosis, planning, and post-arrival information.
missingSources: No separately collected patient directory, PDS/FHIR identity record, site workspace, NHS adapter, direct endpoint, simulation clock, or provenance index is included in this adapted snapshot.
No post-arrival hospital assessment, treatment, response, discharge outcome, medication list, problem list, functional assessment, or advance-planning document is present.
contradictions: Serial creatinine values fall from 50 to 9 micromol/L while reported eGFR falls from 78 to 51 mL/min/1.73m2; this internally unusual pattern should be checked rather than interpreted as a reliable renal trajectory.
Some resource timestamps extend across 2025-2026, while the snapshot cutoff is 2026-09-01; all cited actionable evidence was checked to be on or before the cutoff.
